title: Geometric depth under localization
plausible_today: Keep the invariant defined by a complete regular presentation and its minimal relation count; first establish the excellent/complete and lci cases before expanding quantifiers.
state_of_art: SGA2 XIV5.3–5.6 defines the invariant and proves its étale comparison in characteristic zero; Illusie2003 §1–2 gives relative-depth results over fields and traits. No exact all-noetherian theorem matching this short lemma was located.
why_open: The manuscript says to give proofs; no source explains why this lemma was not expanded on the sheet.
worth: Worth a focused proof-and-hypothesis task because it controls several later dimension bounds.

title: Flat-map geometric depth and the residue hypothesis
as_he_states: Prove5.3.3(ii), and decide whether the formally smooth residue-field realization condition is unnecessary.
plausible_today: Formulate the exact inequality for flat local noetherian maps using Cohen factorizations, retaining any separability/completion hypotheses actually needed.
state_of_art: SGA2 XIV5.5 treats flat local maps with separable residue-field fibre; Illusie2003 supplies the finite-type relative setting. The unrestricted removal in this draft was not matched exactly.
why_open: The writer explicitly doubts the extra condition and leaves both demonstrations for later.
worth: Worth one bounded commutative-algebra audit; the finite-type case alone must not be sold as the full answer.

title: Nonabelian local Lefschetz specialization
as_he_states: Replace the lci hypothesis by geometric depth≥3 and obtain low-degree noncommutative specialization.
plausible_today: Use prime-to-residue-characteristic ind-finite torsors and the precise depth and base assumptions of the local Lefschetz theorem.
state_of_art: Raynaud1974 III1.2–1.3 gives the checked comparison; Orgogozo2003 §3–4 removes resolution assumptions for several generic prime-to-p results. The SGA2 XIV6.2 editorial note points to Raynaud; it is not a licence to erase all hypotheses in6.3.
why_open: The sheet explicitly makes the extension conditional on SGA2 XIV6.3; its printed reference is misnumbered SGA1.
worth: Worth a precise theorem concordance, with no assumption that the broadest excellent-base reading remains open.

title: Acyclicity from singular-locus dimension over a local base
as_he_states: For excellent flat local A→B, predict local(m−d−1)-acyclicity and a degree-one nonabelian analogue.
plausible_today: Separate the trait lci theorem from the higher-dimensional-base formulation, specifying geometric singular loci after residue extensions and prime-to-p coefficients.
state_of_art: SGA7 I4.5–4.8 and Illusie2003 establish the trait depth/lci range; Raynaud1974 and Orgogozo2003 give the cited nonabelian subcases. Full quantifier identity was not established.
why_open: Resolution and local Lefschetz input are explicitly proposed, not supplied.
worth: Worth an exact-scope historical audit before posing any new research problem.

title: Stable marked models and the residue-field question
as_he_states: Use a nontrivial model theorem to be proved later; ask whether the residue field must be perfect.
plausible_today: Use stable marked reduction after a finite extension under the actual trait hypotheses, and distinguish the proof’s reduction of residue fields from the theorem’s statement.

title: A fixed square in Bertini with a prescribed section
as_he_states: The marginal suggestion is that the square should suffice in the hyperplane reduction.
plausible_today: A correct sufficient-large-power theorem with prescribed section and boundary transversality; any uniform exponent2 needs its own hypotheses or counterexample.
state_of_art: SGA7 I5.5 states the generic-section reduction; Orgogozo2003 Th4.10 gives a prime-to-p Lefschetz theorem. Neither verifies this exact exponent2 proposal.
why_open: The source says to explain more and points to EGA V, which is not a published volume.
worth: Potentially useful as a small sharp-bound audit, after the line bundle and embedding assumptions are recovered from the scan.

title: Reference for compact analytic linearity
as_he_states: A margin asks for a reference to faithful linear representations of compact Qell-analytic groups.
plausible_today: Every such compact group is linear over Qell, using local Ado integration and finite-index induction.
state_of_art: Lazard1965 is the earlier theory; Casals-Ruiz–Zozaya2025 Th2.1 supplies a checked primary proof and degree bound for uniform groups plus induction.
why_open: The question is bibliographical, not evidence that the author doubted or invented the theorem.
worth: Resolve in commentary with an exact citation; it does not warrant a new research project.

title: Analytic and algebraic envelope comparison
as_he_states: The page asks when the analytic and algebraic objects agree and leaves an exceptional-case speculation.
plausible_today: Separate equality of analytic Lie algebras, openness in a Zariski closure, full rational-point groups, and reconstruction with a fibre functor.
state_of_art: Deligne–Milne2.8–2.11 proves the reconstruction; local Lie theory proves the openness criterion. The tentative unqualified progroup-isomorphism assertion is not identifiable as a settled theorem in that wording.
why_open: The writer marks a question and then drops two subsequent remarks; no later source is used to infer a motive.
worth: Worth a concise counterexample table and notation audit, not an invented classification theorem.

title: The deferred infinite-dimension claim
as_he_states: The source promises that both analytic and algebraic dimensions are always infinite.
plausible_today: Algebraic quotient dimensions are unbounded for the procyclic arithmetic example, but analytic Lie dimension can be1.
state_of_art: The complete Spec(Fbar_p) counterexample and exponential-character proof are supplied in this run; their ingredients are p-adic Lie theory and neutral Tannakian reconstruction.
why_open: The claim is deferred on195 and the continuation196 proves only the algebraic side; no textual retraction is present.
worth: Worth recording as a resolved correction and a pedagogical example, not pursuing as an open conjecture.

title: Arithmetic descent of geometric local systems and fixed quotients
as_he_states: The source expects the local systems and homomorphisms met in geometry to descend, and hopes to realize a useful fixed quotient at one model.
plausible_today: A proper smooth finite-presentation family and finitely many algebraic maps/correspondences descend to some model; arbitrary lisse ell-adic systems need not.
state_of_art: Stacks01ZM with finite/étale descent gives finite-presentation descent; centralizers at a fixed representation stabilize after the finite component issue is removed. No theorem quantifying over “everything met in practice” is inferred.
why_open: This is a methodological hope in6.16–6.17, not an explicit arbitrary-local-system conjecture.
worth: Useful for explaining the manuscript’s arithmetic model category with one concrete family.

title: Tate endomorphisms for the arithmetic model pro-group
as_he_states: End(A)⊗Qell should equal the commutant of the arithmetic pro-group for normal integral X.
plausible_today: Keep the model category, ell invertibility and normal-base hypotheses; after descent the equality is the Tate homomorphism theorem.
state_of_art: Gajda–Petersen2022/2023 Th2.3 states the all-finitely-generated-field theorem and Lemma3.4 the normal-base extension. Zarhin2010/2011 identifies the Tate1966, Zarhin1975–76, Faltings1983–84 and Mori1985 characteristic-specific history.
why_open: The manuscript already knows Tate’s finite-field case. The sources establish the later cases; they do not explain this appendix’s editorial fate.
worth: Worth a historical completion note, not a surviving instance of the general Tate conjecture.

title: Ell-independence of the normal-crossing weight complexes
as_he_states: Under the standard conjectures, dimensions and Frobenius polynomials of the specified weight pieces should be independent ofell.
plausible_today: Identify the exact restriction/Gysin complex and rank statement; prove a selected case using a known realization or a verified standard-conjecture hypothesis.
state_of_art: WeilII proves purity and weight degeneration. Van Dobben de Bruyn2020 Theorem1,p3 proves the exact equivalence over Fbar_p between homological-equivalence independence, ranks of algebraic correspondences and compact-support Betti independence for all separated finite-type schemes. His introduction pp2–3 treats this SNC/hypercover argument. The equivalent assertions remain conjectural; Wan–Zhang §1.1,p2 confirms the general open scope.
why_open: The source explicitly writes the standard-conjecture condition and the unchecked d2 identification.
worth: High interest, but a short run should produce a precise reduction and known-case map rather than announce a solution of a standard conjecture.

title: Duality and motivic identification of d2
as_he_states: The page tentatively compares the two complexes and leaves compatibility of the motivic d2 maps to check.

state_of_art: The normal-crossing Kummer calculation and Weil purity justify the page bound, while SGA7/Illusie provide the nearby-cycle framework. The exact handwritten compatibility still needs a typed coherent diagram.
why_open: The verification is explicitly postponed; no claim of a failed proof is inferred.
worth: High value for one research run because it is a finite comparison of named maps and signs.

title: Purity of inertia invariants and coinvariants
as_he_states: The displayed conclusion suggests both are pure of the cohomological weight.
plausible_today: Replace the false invariant/coinvariant assertion by the accurately formulated monodromy-weight filtration statement in an identified geometric class.
state_of_art: The split Tate elliptic curve refutes the literal claim. Illusie2021 §6 reviews weight–monodromy; Ito–Zou’s author preprint dated2026-10-06 proves the hyper-Kähler case, not the general conjecture.
why_open: The source makes the conclusion conditional on its preceding construction; the counterexample shows that the condition cannot justify this literal consequence.
worth: Worth a precise correction and example; do not promote the false sentence into a new open problem.
